subject: Pilot SLO validation: dedicated GPU tiering, sizing checklist & demo actions
messages:
From: Mark Oppenheimer <mark.oppenheimer@medicore.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Feb 2028 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot SLO validation for dedicated capacity – next steps

Hi Nikhil / Lauren,

Thanks for the call today — good alignment overall. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying questions so we can lock the pilot window: 

Summary of what we need to validate in the pilot:
- Achieve p95 generation latency <= 180ms for short-form prompts (<= 256 tokens) under steady-state traffic.
- Sustained throughput of 150–200 req/s for inference with 4 concurrent model instances; burst to 400 req/s for short periods.
- Streaming support for long-form summarization (clients expect partial token delivery; target start-of-stream latency < 100ms).
- Support for per-request KV cache affinity for sessionized chat workloads.

Clarifying items we didn't capture precisely on the call:
1) For the p95 target above, is the 180ms measured on token-start or end-of-stream? We mean end-of-stream in our SLA wording.
2) We will provide a representative subset of our dataset (attached) and a mocked client stream pattern. Do you need a different format?
3) Any recommended GPU tier shortlists you think will give the best cost/perf trade for our mix?

Next steps we propose from Medicore: share the sanitized pilot dataset and open a 60-minute slot for the benchmark.

Attachments: pilot_dataset_sample.csv (sample of 1k requests)

Thanks,
Mark Oppenheimer
Head of Platform Engineering
Medicore Health

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Mark Oppenheimer <mark.oppenheimer@medicore.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Feb 2028 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot SLO validation for dedicated capacity – next steps

Hi Mark — thanks for the clear summary and for the attached sample. Quick answers and our asks to make the pilot efficient: 

1) SLA measurement: we measure p95 on end-of-stream (full-response latency). We'll run both token-start and end-of-stream during the bench and report both, but will gate sizing on end-of-stream as you requested.

2) Dataset format: CSV is fine. If possible, include a column with session_id and a streaming_flag to indicate which rows should simulate chunked streaming. That lets us validate streaming start-of-stream latency separately.

3) GPU tier recommendations (high-level):
   - H100 80GB (best perf): lowest latency for large-context streaming and highest throughput; higher per-hour cost. Best if you need aggressive concurrency + KV cache per session.
   - A100 80GB (balanced): solid throughput with predictable behavior for standard models; generally best price/perf for non-LLM-bleeding-edge needs.
   - L4 / T4 family (infer): lower cost but expect higher tail latency on large context / streaming; okay for cheap embeddings or light workloads.

For sizing: based on your call profile (150–200 rps steady, bursts to 400), our initial estimate is: reserve a mid-size dedicated pool equivalent to 6 x A100-80GB (or 4 x H100-80GB if you prioritize latency), with autoscaled burst capacity to add 2–3 additional cards for short bursts. Exact numbers depend on model variant, sequence lengths, and quantization.

Pilot logistics we need from you:
- Final sanitized dataset and streaming flag (CSV) — you already attached a sample, great.
- Expected model family (open or fine-tuned) and sequence length distribution.
- A suggested 60-minute benchmark slot via Calendly (we can run two back-to-back bench runs).

I'll have Lauren and Priyom scope a concise bench plan and a checklist we can use during the slot.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Director, Solution Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Mark Oppenheimer <mark.oppenheimer@medicore.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Feb 2028 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot SLO validation for dedicated capacity – bench plan & GPU shortlist

Mark — looping in a short bench plan and GPU shortlist so we can be aligned for the run. See inline.

Bench plan (30–60m actual runs):
- Pre-bench (15m): deploy two model variants (quantized and FP16) to dedicated pool, warm KV caches with a 5-minute prefix run.
- Run 1 (20m steady-state): steady injection at target 160 rps, concurrency pattern to 4 concurrent sessions, measure p50/p95/p99 end-of-stream latencies and per-token streaming start latency.
- Run 2 (10m burst): short 2–3 minute bursts to 400 rps, observe latency cliffs and autoscale behavior.
- Post-bench (10m): log collection, quick triage and recommended configuration determination.

GPU shortlist rationale:
- H100 (config A): best for your streaming + large-context needs — expect 20–30% lower p95 vs A100 on identical configs. Good for p95 < 150ms targets.
- A100 (config B): most predictable and cost-efficient for 150–220 rps workloads on our current model variants when using FP16 or 4-bit quant.
- Hybrid (config C): reserve A100s for steady state, keep 1–2 H100s in the burst pool for latency-sensitive traffic — gives a middle ground on cost while preserving p95 for short spikes.

Sizing checklist (what we'll produce after the bench):
- Recommended dedicated pool spec (card counts by type)
- Expected steady-state RPS and safe burst headroom
- Autoscaling policy thresholds and cold-start assumptions
- Estimated monthly committed cost (reserved + burst ops) and per-token cost delta between choices

Attachments: pilot_requirements.xlsx (checklist and benchmark scripts)

I'll send a calendar invite for Friday at 10:00am PST. If that doesn't work for you, use the Calendly link and we can shift.

—Lauren
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
